processing: Pan-fired by hand or machine and pressed flat in the wok, in the Long Jing manner, with no oxidation.
harvest_season: Spring. As with all Long Jing, pre-Qingming picking is the most prized, followed by lots picked before Guyu.
appearance_dry: Flat, smooth blades in green to yellowish green, varying by cultivar and maker.
appearance_wet: Tender flat shoots in soft green.
taste_profile: A Long Jing cup, typically chestnut and bean-sweet with a clean finish; cultivar and picking shift it, and Zhenong 117 leans higher in aroma.

brewing.notes: Typical Long Jing handling: a glass or open gaiwan, water around 80 C, and do not leave the leaves sitting in water.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring tea, priced by picking date: pre-Qingming lots first and dearest, then pre-Guyu. It is the volume side of Long Jing, so grade and date matter a great deal. Drink within the year and store it cold and sealed.
description:
Yuezhou Longjing is not a single tea but one of three legal Long Jing production zones, alongside Xihu and Qiantang. It covers the Shaoxing area, including Xinchang, Shengzhou and Zhuji, and runs into parts of neighbouring counties such as Dongyang, Pan'an and Tiantai.

The method is the flat wok-pressed Long Jing method. What differs is scale and cultivar: Longjing Changye and Zhenong 117 are named as main plants here, and Zhenong 117 is known for a higher aroma.

Expect the Long Jing register of chestnut and sweet beans, usually at a gentler price than West Lake tea. As with all Long Jing, cooler water and a short steep keep it sweet.

The key buying point is legal: only tea from the West Lake zone may be called Xihu Longjing. Yuezhou tea is sold as Long Jing, Yuezhou Longjing or under local names such as Dafo Longjing. Good lots can be excellent value, so ask for county and date.

If you want to learn the category, compare a pre-Qingming lot from here with one from Qiantang and from West Lake side by side.
history:
The zones are set out by the national standard for Long Jing as a geographical indication product. A Hangzhou press report calls Yuezhou the largest zone by output, though exact shares differ between sources.

The zone's name comes from the old prefecture of Yue.
